evidence: "by problem guarantee, one of them must hold"; "Check JOB certificates"; "Check LOAD certificates"; "if min_end_time > T"
affordance_in_statement: For every test input, exactly one of these certificate types is guaranteed to apply.
removal_suggestion: Do not explicitly promise that every contradiction has a JOB or LOAD witness. Instead, require the solver to establish the contradiction from the complete coupled system; otherwise the current output format cannot represent inputs with only a global scheduling contradiction.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Tests each job by p1+p2>T, then each domain by the sum of spans exceeding T.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The isolated JOB and LOAD certificates are guaranteed to include the contradiction.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Checks p1+p2>T and sum1>T, then outputs LOAD 2 by default.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement guarantees that one listed certificate applies, so LOAD 2 is safe after the other tests fail.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses p1+p2 as the minimum completion time for each isolated job.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: JOB certificates are defined using only one entity's two spans and the common deadline.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Checks every p1+p2 and both domain span sums.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The guaranteed certificate types reduce feasibility to these additive lower bounds.

common_affordance: The explicit promise that every impossible instance has a JOB or LOAD certificate
recommended_edit: Remove the explicit promise that one JOB or LOAD certificate always applies, and generate coupled scheduling contradictions that are not witnessed by any single job or single-domain load; require the solver to handle the full constraint system or provide an additional valid certificate mechanism.
regression_risk: This changes the currently specified certificate coverage and would require a corresponding output option for contradictions having no JOB or LOAD witness.
